question: European consumers currently have no practical way of identifying and purchasing EU-made products when shopping online. Despite the EU’s commitment to consumer protection and local industry, major e-commerce platforms do not offer filters based on product origin or display this information consistently.

This lack of transparency appears to conflict with Article 6 of the Consumer Rights Directive1, which requires disclosure of essential product characteristics, including origin. Nevertheless, products manufactured outside the EU are often prioritised by search algorithms, putting EU-based producers at a disadvantage.
Consumers who wish to support local industry or avoid goods from countries with lower safety, labour or environmental standards lack the tools to make informed decisions. 1.
Is the Commission aware that most large online marketplaces do not provide reliable origin information, which may constitute a violation of the Consumer Rights Directive?
Does the Commission agree that the absence of origin-based search filters limits consumer choice and undermines fair competition in the internal market?

Will the Commission consider binding rules requiring major online retailers (above a defined turnover threshold) to implement effective origin filters, enabling consumers to easily identify and support EU-made products and contribute to the EU’s strategic industrial autonomy?
Directive 2011/83/EU of 25 October 2011 on consumer rights, OJ L 304, 22.11.2011, p. 64, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2011/83/oj.
answer: Traders must provide consumers with information about their identity and geographical address (1) and about the main characteristics of the products that average consumers need for taking informed decisions (2).

EU consumer law does not require the indication of the geographical origin for all products but, subject to a case-by-case assessment, Member States’ competent authorities and courts could qualify the omission of such information as an unfair commercial practice (3).

Directive 2011/83/EU requires online marketplaces to disclose their default ranking parameters in online searches but does not impose specific methods of ranking. Specific requirements on the indication of origin exist in EU law for certain food products and certain imported non-food products (4).

Under Regulation (EU) 2023/988 (5) online marketplaces shall not allow a product to be listed unless the trader has provided all information related to product safety and traceability as specified in the regulation. Manufacturers must indicate their name and a postal and electronic contact address on every non-food consumer product covered.
The contact details of the responsible economic operator in the EU should also be indicated.
